259.h: The Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) is a federal university established by the Federal Government of Nigeria in 1981, during the period when the government set up universities of technology in several regions. Its main library, the Albert Ilemobade Library, was established in 1982 and is named after Professor Albert Ilemobade, the university's second vice-chancellor.
259.a: FUTA is organised into schools rather than faculties, together with a College of Health Sciences. The schools cover basic medical sciences, clinical sciences, computing, life sciences, physical sciences, earth and mineral sciences (including applied geophysics, marine science, meteorology and climate science, and remote sensing), environmental technology, electrical and systems engineering, infrastructure, minerals and manufacturing engineering, agriculture and agricultural technology, and logistics and innovation technology, plus a School of Postgraduate Studies. It also runs pre-degree science programmes and short courses.
259.c: The university is located in Akure, the capital of Ondo State. The main library stands beside the engineering school on the main campus.

239.h: Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University (COOU) is a public university owned by the Anambra State Government. It was established as Anambra State University by Law No. 13 of 2000, which phased out the state polytechnic and transferred its assets to the new university. On 11 September 2014 the Anambra State House of Assembly renamed it after Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu, the former military governor of the Eastern Region and leader of the breakaway Republic of Biafra.
239.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine.
239.c: The university has two campuses. One is at Uli, on the former site of Anambra State Polytechnic (Ekwenugo Okeke Polytechnic). The other is at Igbariam, in Anambra East local government area, on the former site of the state College of Agriculture, which shared the site with the university until it moved to Mgbakwu, about 15 kilometres away, in 2006.

274.h: Gombe State University (GSU) is a public university owned by the Gombe State Government. It was set up under Governor Mohammed Danjuma Goje: the state ministry of education convened a 35-member stakeholders' committee, and the executive council then appointed a 24-member technical planning committee to establish it. The National Universities Commission records 2004. Its first vice-chancellor was Professor Abdullahi Mahadi. The university has no religious affiliation, and as a state university its tuition and accommodation costs are relatively low.
274.a: GSU's faculties include Arts and Social Sciences, with departments such as accounting, business administration, economics, history, international relations, peace and conflict resolution and public administration; Education, which pairs teacher training with subjects such as physics, biology, chemistry, mathematics and computer science; Environmental Sciences; and medicine. It is a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities.
274.c: The main campus is at Tudun Wada, in the Shamaki ward of Gombe. The Faculty of Environmental Sciences is on a separate campus at Dukku.

338.h: The University of Jos (UNIJOS) grew out of a satellite campus of the University of Ibadan, set up in Jos in November 1971. Its first students were admitted to pre-degree courses in January 1972, and a Bachelor of Arts programme began in October 1973. In October 1975 the military government of General Murtala Mohammed made it a separate university, with Professor Gilbert Onuaguluchi as its first vice-chancellor. Teaching at the new university began in October 1976 with 575 students in four faculties: Arts and Social Sciences, Education, Natural Sciences and Medical Sciences.
338.a: Postgraduate programmes were added in 1977, and by 1978 faculties of Law and Environmental Sciences had been created. Today UNIJOS offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most disciplines, including medicine. In 2003 the Carnegie Corporation of New York gave the university a US$2 million grant to build its own fundraising office.
338.c: The university is in Jos, the capital of Plateau State. Its library, founded in 1962 while the institution was still part of Ibadan, is on Bauchi Road opposite the Federal College of Forestry.

212.h: Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko (AAUA) is a public university owned by the Ondo State Government. Its history starts in March 1982, when the government of the old Ondo State under Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin founded a state university, which the following military government renamed Ondo State University in 1985. After Ekiti State was carved out of Ondo State in 1996, the old campus at Ado-Ekiti fell in the new state, and a 1999 law signed by Governor Adebayo Adefarati relocated Ondo's university to Akungba-Akoko. Staff moved to the new site on 1 December 1999. After Ajasin's death, a 2004 law renamed the university in his honour.
212.a: AAUA offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes as well as pre-degree and JUPEB courses, which prepare students for direct entry into degree programmes.
212.c: The university is located in the town of Akungba-Akoko in the Akoko area of northern Ondo State.

344.h: Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS) is a public research university, one of the universities the Federal Government founded in 1975. It is named after Usman dan Fodio, the nineteenth-century scholar and reformer who founded the Sokoto Caliphate.
344.a: UDUS awards four-, five- and six-year degrees, as well as associate degrees and remedial programmes, across fifteen faculties. They include Agriculture; Arts; Arabic and Islamic Studies; Education; Engineering and Environmental Design; Law; Life Sciences; Management Sciences; Social Sciences; Physical and Computing Sciences; Veterinary Medicine; Pharmaceutical Sciences; Dentistry; and Medical Laboratory Science, alongside a College of Health Sciences and a teaching hospital.
344.c: The university uses three campuses in Sokoto. The main campus holds ten faculties, the senate, the Abdullahi Fodiyo Library Complex, which seats more than 4,500 readers, and the School of Postgraduate Studies. The city campus houses veterinary medicine and the veterinary teaching hospital, the Centre for Islamic Studies and the School of Matriculation Studies. A third campus holds the teaching hospital and the health science faculties.

309.h: Olabisi Onabanjo University (OOU) is a public university owned by the Ogun State Government. It was founded on 7 July 1982 as Ogun State University, and many people still call it OSU. On 29 May 2001 it was renamed after Olabisi Onabanjo, the civilian governor of Ogun State whose government established it.
309.a: OOU has ten faculties with 53 departments in all. The Faculty of Science covers chemical sciences, mathematical sciences, microbiology, plant science and applied zoology, physics and earth sciences. Education, Law, Arts, and Administration and Management Sciences are among the others; management sciences include accounting, business administration, transport management, banking and finance, and taxation. The university also teaches medicine.
309.c: The main campus is in Ago-Iwoye, Ogun State, and the faculties are spread across several campuses in the state.

304.h: Niger Delta University (NDU) is a public university funded by the Bayelsa State Government. It was established in 2000 by Chief D. S. P. Alamieyeseigha, then governor of Bayelsa State. It is a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities.
304.a: NDU offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees in thirteen faculties. They include Agricultural Technology (agricultural economics, crop production, fisheries and livestock); Arts; Environmental Sciences (architecture, quantity surveying, building and urban planning); Basic Medical Sciences and Clinical Sciences, which together train doctors; and Engineering, with departments of agricultural, chemical and petroleum, civil, electrical and electronic, and marine engineering, reflecting the state's oil and water-borne economy.
304.c: The main campus is at Amassoma on Wilberforce Island, and the Faculty of Law is in Yenagoa, the state capital. The Niger Delta University Teaching Hospital is at Okolobiri.
